Welcome
Welcome to Beaulieu Village Primary School! My name is Michelle Hale and I am the Headteacher.
We are a highly successful small school at the heart of the historic village of Beaulieu. Our school is a family and our children thrive because staff know them inside out and are passionate about enabling each individual child to achieve excellence and to shine.
Our children take part in very special events and have a range of rich experiences throughout their time with us. They experience belonging to our village, as well as our school, and leave us with unique memories, shining with the confidence that comes from having strong relationships and being known and valued as an individual.
The best way to find out about our beautiful school is to come and visit us, we would love to meet you.
Please click below to find out more about our vision for our children and the values which shape our school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Beaulieu Village Primary School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our Vision
Our vision is of a school family within which each child is inspired to have self-belief, to love learning and to strive for their personal best. We seek to prepare our children to thrive in an uncertain future by teaching them to embrace their own individuality, to form strong relationships with others, to think creatively and to work hard.
Our School Values
Courage is about being honest and standing up for what is right and for what you believe in. Courageous people take brave action when they need to and show the resilience to keep going even when things are tough. We need courage in order to be true to all our values.
Kindness is about caring for yourself and for others. Kind people are compassionate, respectful, inclusive and fair. They value one another as individuals, show emotional intelligence and build positive relationships.
Shining is about individuality, aspiration and creativity. We recognise and value our own individuality and the individuality of others; we have self-belief; we love learning and aspire to improve and to embrace new and exciting experiences; we value thinking creatively and we celebrate ideas.
Our Vision - September 2025 pdf

pageCache.pageTitle: Beaulieu Village Primary School - British Values
pageCache.text:
British Values
British Values In our whole school assemblies this term we are talking about British Values. Schools across the country teach the Fundamental British Values: democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of different faiths and beliefs. These values are promoted through the school curriculum, Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural (SMSC) development, and daily life to create a cohesive society and protect children from extremist ideologies. This Autumn term we are focusing on Democracy. In our We talk about how we encourage democratic practices by teaching the children about the UK's democratic system, allowing them to participate in school governance, and creating an environment where pupil voices are valued and heard. The children have voted for their House and Vice House Captains as well as their year group School Councillors.

pageCache.pageTitle: Beaulieu Village Primary School - New Forest Learning Alliance
pageCache.text:
New Forest Learning Alliance
Beaulieu Village Primary School is proudly part of the New Forest Learning Alliance (NFLA).
We are a group of four autonomous schools who support and challenge one another to create the best outcomes for all our children.
Each school has its own headteacher, its own governing body and its own unique approach. We all value being at the heart of our communities.
Our collaboration provides extra opportunities for our children and increased professional development for our staff.
For Beaulieu, being part of the NFLA allows us to preserve the small school family approach we love, whilst also benefitting from high levels of professional development and support.
Alongside priding ourselves on knowing the children in our small village school “inside out,” we are part of a rich professional community, striving to achieve the highest possible standards.

pageCache.pageTitle: Beaulieu Village Primary School - Our Governors
pageCache.text:
Our Governors
Welcome to our Governors’ section. We are a Governing Body of 10 members made up of Head teacher, 1 staff governor, 1 Local Authority governor, 2 parent governors and 5 co-opted governors. We meet every half term for full governor body meetings (6 per year) and have termly Curriculum Committee meetings. Some members meet for Pay Committee and HT performance management meetings during the year.
Please find below details of how our Governing body is structured, including the names, categories, responsibilities and terms of appointment for each Governor.
Our Clerk, Claire Backhouse, can be contacted for more information on her email address claire.backhouse@hants.gov.uk
Vacancy for School Governor
We currently have a vacancy for a school governor. Please see our full advert at the bottom of the page or contact the school office for more information.
Application Form - School Governor
Find out more about being a school governor in Hampshire visit www.hants.gov.uk/governors-volunteer
https://www.hants.gov.uk/educationandlearning/governors/volunteer/whatgovernorsdo
Andrea Oram
Local Authority Governor
Primary school governor since 2013 (Chair of Governors since 2016)
It was the beautiful surroundings and family-friendly feel that first attracted me to Beaulieu School as a parent. My four boys all loved their time here and often reflect on their unique memories, making the school vision very personal to me. This vested interest was my reason for joining the governing body as a parent governor in 2013. Now as Chair, I am dedicated to ensuring the school meets it long-term goal, and I am passionate that all pupils are equipped with the tools for successful learning.
I find it extremely rewarding to be able to draw on my previous life and work experiences, which include 15 years working in clinical research and data management and 5 years in other volunteering roles (preschool trustee and mother and toddler group leader). Furthermore, my background in science and data handling have provided excellent transferable skills towards the strategic leadership of the school. With a keen interest in understanding more about how children learn, I recently completed 3 years of postgraduate research in education at Southampton University. My research interest is in the theories and complexities of learning to read, with a particular focus on specific word reading difficulties. I completed the Chairs Development Programme with NCTL in 2016.
Michelle Hale
Headteacher Governor.
Fiona Duncan
I love Beaulieu School for the family environment that it provides as a small rural primary. I have a daughter in KS1 and a son in KS2 who are very different, and their teachers are doing a wonderful job of supporting them both as they move up the school. I have seen them grow hugely in confidence in their time here and I know that means they feel very safe. Over the last 4 years I have been an active member of FOBS and the Sailing Club which means I have had the chance to get to know lots of families across all year groups. I think having an active school community, including great links with the local community as we have through the Sailing Club, really strengthens our school. Ongoing open communication between families and the school is a very important part of that.
Kerry Thorne
Co-opted Governor. Safer Recruitment Trained Governor and (DTG)Training Governor
Vacancy
Elizabeth Smith
I joined the governing body in September 2022 as a co-opted governor.
My background is in education, having taught across the primary age range in a variety of schools in Portsmouth, Southampton and Hampshire. I have been a Headteacher of two Primary schools.
I am passionate about the education children receive and have a desire to ensure every child has the best possible education and opportunities on their journey through learning.
Since retiring, I am keen to draw on my experience and skills to work with the whole school community and play an active part in contributing to the continued success of the school.
I have lived and worked in the local area for over 35 years and have been involved in the community through my work and personal interests.
Mark Amey
I joined the governing body in December 2023 as a parent governor. As a person who only found out they were Dyslexic in their late twenties, I felt I would have a unique grasp and insight into the needs of a more challenged child that would serve me well in the position of governor. I am a keen sportsman, in particular rugby, which I have played all my adult life, from representing my local club as Captain to playing for the County and the South of England. I pride myself on my strong team values and on my ethical approach to all situations, including respect for others, a strong sense of fair play and staying calm under pressure. I love Beaulieu Primary School and its staff and the kindness and attention given to my eldest son. I would like to give back to the local community and also see the "other side" of the day to day running of my children's school. I have a genuine care for the continued wellbeing of the staff, school and pupils.
Doug Reid
Co-Opted Governor I have worked as a sports instructor and coach since 2010, teaching adventurous activities such as sailing, windsurfing, and snowsports to children and adults of all ages. This has given me valuable insight into how young people grow in confidence and resilience when faced with challenges. I am passionate about inclusive education and have often supported children with additional needs, including dyslexia, ADHD, and autism. I now mentor younger instructors to ensure they can deliver sessions that meet the needs of all learners. Having lived and worked in the Waterside area since 2019, I feel strongly connected to the local community. I value Beaulieu’s unique offering and am committed to supporting the school in delivering its vision, ensuring that every child benefits from both classroom learning and opportunities to learn outside the classroom.
Rachel Strange
As a trustee and advisory committee member for Beaulieu Young Farmers Club, I am jointly responsible for the governance and management of the club and its activities, ensuring that it operates legally, safely, and in line with its constitution. This experience has strengthened my understanding of good governance practices, compliance, and the importance of safeguarding and accountability in any organisation.
As a former teacher with over 20 years’ experience in education, I bring a strong understanding of how schools operate both strategically and on a day-to-day basis. My teaching background has provided me with extensive experience in curriculum development, assessment, safeguarding, and supporting pupils’ academic and personal growth.
Overall, I am passionate about contributing to the continued success of Beaulieu School and ensuring that every child has the opportunity to thrive within its caring and close-knit community.
Caroline Cunningham

TV presenter, teacher and parent Michael Underwood has teamed up with White Rose maths team to film a mini-series called Maths with Michael which covers a range of topics: place value, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, fractions and algebra (so there's something relevant to each year group). Curriculum
Curriculum Statement - March 2026
Our curriculum is inspirational, designed to fire our children’s curiosity and love of learning.
It is underpinned by our school values and our British values and makes the most of our beautiful and historic setting, our place at the heart of our village community and the family feel of our school.
We pride ourselves on knowing our children “inside out” and using this knowledge to individualise learning. Our children build strong relationships within our school family but also learn to be uniquely themselves.
Through our nurturing environment we teach our children to have courage, be kind and shine. They also learn about leadership, with all our children being supported to take up positions of responsibility before they leave us.
A culture of excellence underlies our curriculum. Learning in each subject is a “journey to excellence,” broken down into small steps. We have high expectations of all our children and strive to capture and celebrate excellence from each of them. We teach children about the importance of effort and resilience.
Children’s learning and teachers’ understanding of children are strengthened immeasurably when we are able to work in close partnership with parents and carers. Our school has an "Open Door" policy, and we warmly welcome questions and feedback about what children are learning through informal conversations with parents at the end of the school day. Teachers provide information about what children are learning each half term and curriculum evenings and workshops take place every year.
We follow the National Curriculum for all subjects and make use of some published schemes to support our planning.
Each subject is led by a member of staff with knowledge and passion about that subject. Our teachers use teaching approaches which are rooted in research and as a staff we keep up to date with current thinking and constantly reflect on our practice and on the needs of our children.
Schemes which support our curriculum
Children in the Early Years and in Key Stage One follow the Little Wandle programme to support their phonics learning and learning to read
To help support the teaching of spelling we use the Bridge to Spelling programme
To help support the teaching of handwriting we use Letterjoin
To help support the teaching of maths and science we use White Rose Education
To support our teaching of computing we use Purple Mash
To support our music teaching we use Kapow Primary
To support our teaching of French and Spanish we use Language Angels
Jigsaw supports our personal, social, emotional and health education
To support our teaching of PE we use Primary PE Planning
If you have any questions about our curriculum, please do not hesitate to contact us.

SEND
Special Education Needs (and/or) Disabilities (SEND)
At Beaulieu Primary School we endeavour to meet the academic, social and physical needs of each and every child in our care by being a fully inclusive school. Through quality teaching and an engaging curriculum, we support all children to become successful throughout their learning journey with us and beyond. However, there may be occasions when your child may need additional support in order for them to achieve their full potential and it is our duty to ensure we meet their needs at the earliest possible moment.
The SENCO at Beaulieu Primary is Charlotte Stroud.
Local & School Offer
Our school's Special Educational Needs Report and Policy outlines how we provide for SEND children in our school. Our SEN Policy can be found on our policies page

pageCache.pageTitle: Beaulieu Village Primary School - Forest School
pageCache.text:
Forest School
“Forest School is an inspirational process that offers children, young people and adults’ regular opportunities to achieve and develop confidence and self-esteem through hands on learning.”
Forest Education Initiative
Our School Vision Our vision is of a school family within which each child is inspired to have self-belief, to love learning and to strive for excellence. We seek to prepare our children to thrive in an uncertain future by teaching them to embrace their own individuality, to form strong relationships with others, to think creatively and to work hard.
Our ‘Forest School Vision’ focuses on creating a positive learning environment, tailored to suit the individual needs and learning styles that maximize the emotional, social and developmental benefits of education that help children build positive values about themselves, their learning and the environment.
Activities take place outdoors, in small groups with a high staffing ratio. The programme is long term, regular and frequent and learning is automatically enhanced as the outdoor environment naturally offers an environment that is informal, challenging, unpredictable and stimulating. This allows the participants the opportunity to test and maintain their curiosity of the world around them as they explore using multiple senses.
The learning and teaching strategies used foster independence and develop language and communication skills and increase levels of physical activity and emotional wellbeing. Time is given to explore their thoughts, feelings and relationships and they are encouraged to understand, appreciate, care and connect with the natural environment.
Opportunities are provided to take risks, make choices, find new ways of working, initiate learning, develop practical skills and become confident and capable individuals by giving them challenging but achievable tasks and the time to reflect on this.
At Beaulieu Village Primary we are lucky to have a large field and fenced ‘Wild Area’ to provide a variety of outdoor learning opportunities. Forest school compliments our school values.
